title: All Things Are Lawful For Me
body:
15 Minutes w/ The Captains · 2026-09-18

Opens [1 Cor 6](/bible/1-corinthians/6) · [Matt 18](/bible/matthew/18) · [Matt 23](/bible/matthew/23) · [Ps 148](/bible/psalms/148) · [1 Cor 1](/bible/1-corinthians/1)
## Introduction *[[0:21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=21s)]* Today's class is on something the Apostle Paul said in 1 Corinthians 6:12: all things are lawful for me. The Christian church took it and ran with it, and they ran off the cliff with it. We are here today to give you the proper understanding and reel you back in. There is no possible way we can have a clear understanding of 1 Corinthians 6:12 if we don't have a clue what is happening in 1 Corinthians 6:1. ## Scriptures Opened **[1 Corinthians 6:1](/bible/1-corinthians/6#v1)** *[[1:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=61s)]* > [1](/bible/1-corinthians/6#v1) Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints? - Dare any of you, having a matter against another: what would a matter against another look like? That's a problem, an issue, a trespass, a sin between brothers and sisters inside the congregation. - But Christ already gave us the source. He gave us the blueprint on how to resolve issues in Matthew 18:15-17. **[Matthew 18:15-17](/bible/matthew/18#v15)** *[[1:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=90s)]* > [15](/bible/matthew/18#v15) Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother. > > [16](/bible/matthew/18#v16) But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. > > [17](/bible/matthew/18#v17) And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican. - If thy brother shall trespass against thee: if a brother breaks a commandment, or he does something evil or something wrong, what did Christ say? Step one: go to that brother, go to that sister, and resolve that issue. - Step two: take one or two people with you as witnesses to get that matter resolved. - Step three: tell it to the church, to the leaders in the congregation, to resolve the matter. - So that's the three-step process Christ gave us. Go to the other individual one on one. If that doesn't work, bring one or two people with you as a witness. If that still doesn't work, you take it to the leadership inside the congregation to get the matter resolved. - But when we get to 1 Corinthians, the church has been established in Corinth, and Christ has died, resurrected and gone back to the heavens. Now the church in Corinth wants to come up with a new formula, because they figured it out better than Christ. **[1 Corinthians 6:1](/bible/1-corinthians/6#v1)** *[[3:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=198s)]* > [1](/bible/1-corinthians/6#v1) Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints? - Go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints: these brothers and sisters were having issues inside the congregation and decided to step outside the congregation to deal with unjust men to resolve their issues, instead of dealing with the saints, the people inside the congregation, the leaders of the congregation. - Now, who are those unjust men that people were going to law with? Christ already told us who the unjust are in Matthew 23. **[Matthew 23:2](/bible/matthew/23#v2)** *[[3:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=239s)]* > [2](/bible/matthew/23#v2) Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: - The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. What seat is that? That's the seat of judgment, the seat of justice. But the Bible says that these are unjust men. **[Matthew 23:23](/bible/matthew/23#v23)** *[[4:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=265s)]* > [23](/bible/matthew/23#v23) Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. - Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites. So if a hypocrite is sitting in Moses' seat, the seat of judgment, authority and justice, what's going to happen? Unjust things are going to happen. Hypocritical things are going to happen. - Ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin: see what the scribes and Pharisees focused on? They focused on those tithes, because they got the benefit from it. - And have omitted the weightier matters of the law, like judgment. So why would I go to the scribes and Pharisees to get a matter judged, when Christ already told us that they omit judgment? - If they omit judgment, you know what another word for that is? Justice. There is no justice amongst these men. So Paul is describing these scribes and Pharisees as the unjust that people are going to law with to get matters resolved. - But now, who are the saints? You might think these white people that's painted on the wall in your Christian church are saints. They not saints. You might think your grandmama that's eating pork, shrimp, crab and lobster is a saint. She ain't no saint. Lord willing she repent, she can be a saint one day. **[Psalms 148:14](/bible/psalms/148#v14)** *[[5:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=359s)]* > [14](/bible/psalms/148#v14) He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord. - The praise of all his saints. Who are the saints? Even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. That's music to my ears right there. - The children of Israel are the saints the Bible is talking about. So if you're not of the children of Israel, if you're not of the 12 tribes of Israel, you ain't no saint. That's what the Bible is telling us. - But the scribes and the Pharisees were Israelites, and the Apostle Paul made a distinction: they didn't fall on the side of the saints. They fell on the side of the unjust. **[1 Corinthians 1:2](/bible/1-corinthians/1#v2)** *[[7:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=428s)]* > [2](/bible/1-corinthians/1#v2) Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours: - Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus: the people that are in the church in Corinth are also the people that are sanctified by Christ. - Called to be saints: the people outside the church weren't called to be saints. The people inside the church are called to be saints. - These people that are called saints were sanctified by Jesus Christ, and they call upon the name of Jesus Christ. So the saints in 1 Corinthians 6:1 are the followers of Christ that are inside the congregation. **[1 Corinthians 6:6](/bible/1-corinthians/6#v6)** *[[8:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=505s)]* > [6](/bible/1-corinthians/6#v6) But brother goeth to law with brother, and that before the unbelievers. - Brother goeth to law with brother, and that before the unbelievers: the brothers are going to have matters judged amongst people that don't believe on Christ. - That makes no sense at all. Why would I go to people that don't believe on Christ to have a matter judged inside the congregation? **[1 Corinthians 6:12](/bible/1-corinthians/6#v12)** *[[8:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=537s)]* > [12](/bible/1-corinthians/6#v12) All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any. - All things are lawful unto me: now we get to the point where the Christian falls off the cliff. What things is Paul talking about in 1 Corinthians 6 that would be lawful? - There's no commandment that says I can't go deal with the Pharisees for matters of judgment. Matter of fact, Christ said all that they bid thee, that observe and do, just don't follow after their works. So I'm not in the midst of sin for going to deal with the Pharisees. - But all things are not expedient. Meaning what? It is not wise for me to go to someone that is a hypocrite, that omits the weightier matters of the law, to judge a matter between two brothers or two sisters that are inside the congregation following Christ. - If the Bible doesn't say that I can't do it, if there's no thou shalt not, then it's lawful. - But I will not be brought under the power of any: since the law doesn't say thou shalt not go to the Pharisees, Paul is telling us that it's lawful. But Paul is also telling us he has enough wisdom not to be brought under the power of the scribes and the Pharisees, because they are hypocritical men. - So all things are lawful: they ain't talking about going to eat shrimp, crab and lobster. It ain't talking about you can celebrate birthdays, Christmas, New Year's in the dead of winter. No. All of those things are unlawful. You're not allowed to do those things according to the Bible. ## In Closing *[[10:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8&t=651s)]* But when we have issues amongst each other inside the congregation, the wisdom is go to the leaders of the congregation. I'm Captain Yahoshua. Until next time, shalom. --- [15 Minutes Index](/captains) · [Watch the full session on YouTube ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KIQ3-c-qwa8)
